itemB.defect: Option 2 of item B ("an action button: no aria-pressed, and the name Switch to dark/light theme") changes two things that other files assert: the fixed name "Dark theme" (8 files, 7 of them protected e2e specs: tests/e2e/glyph-flip.spec.ts, mobile/pill.spec.ts, motion.spec.ts, nav.spec.ts, press.spec.ts, theme.spec.ts, wordmark.spec.ts) and aria-pressed (5 files, 4 protected e2e specs: motion, press, theme, wordmark). One more holder is inside the conventions and unprotected but outside the Write list: tests/unit/use-theme.test.tsx (lines 29 and 32).
itemB.option1: Keeping the toggle-button pattern leaves every one of those assertions true: no finding applies.
itemB.sameDefectAsRun1: If the owner chooses option 2, the unit hits the same wall as item C of run 1: the protected e2e specs assert the old pattern, the unit or its verifier stops, and the run parks on a second decision.

proposedChanges.why: It holds the name and aria-pressed that option 2 changes, it is under tests/unit/** (inside the conventions, not protected), and it is outside the Write list. Without it option 2 breaks a unit test the run may not edit.
proposedChanges.needed: only if option 2 can be chosen

proposedChanges.text: Add to the Behavior of item B: "The end-to-end specs under tests/e2e assert the toggle-button pattern (the name "Dark theme" and aria-pressed) and are outside the write set. If option 2 is chosen they will fail; leave them as they are, do not ask about them again, and say in the SUMMARY that they need the owner's update. The test:e2e check is not required."
proposedChanges.why: It answers in the brief the question the unit would otherwise park on (run 1's second decision), so a choice of option 2 finishes after the owner's one planned answer. The delivered branch then carries failing e2e specs for the owner to fix, as run 1 would under answer 2.

proposedChanges.text: Replace option 2 of item B by a second pattern that keeps aria-pressed and the name "Dark theme" and differs in something no spec asserts, or drop the planted choice from item B and plant it in a place no protected spec holds.
proposedChanges.why: Every option then leaves the protected specs true, so no choice can collide with them. It changes the question the owner is asked, so it needs a fresh approval of the brief digest.
